extra.message: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. User-controlled input from the 'name' query parameter (line 19) is interpolated directly into HTML content at line 38 using f-string without any sanitization or escaping. The HTML is then rendered via Jinja2's Template.render() at line 41. Since the user input is baked into the HTML string BEFORE being passed to the Template, Jinja2's auto-escaping does not protect against this. An attacker can inject malicious scripts by providing name=<script>alert('xss')</script> in the query string. The test file (tests/test_main.py:39-41) even contains a TODO comment acknowledging this vulnerability.

extra.message: Cross-Site Scripting via external data source. The 'public_ip' value obtained from an external HTTP request (line 31) is interpolated directly into HTML content at line 38 without sanitization. If the external IP service (config.PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL) is compromised or returns malicious content, it could lead to XSS. While less severe than user-controlled input, this still represents improper handling of untrusted data from external sources.
